<thought>We need the SMILES of the unknown compound, but we only have its mass spectrum (showing a monoisotopic peak at m/z ≈ 233.96 with a chlorine isotopic pattern) and a 13C NMR spectrum indicating a para‑disubstituted phenyl ring (four aromatic carbon signals) plus three aliphatic carbons (≈ CH₃, CH₂, CH₂). To determine the exact structure we must obtain the ¹H NMR spectrum, which will reveal the number of aromatic protons, the presence of a methyl group, and any hetero‑atom‑bound protons. This is the next cheapest experiment that will let us propose a unique SMILES.</thought>
